subject: physics
question_text: State Kepler’s laws of planetary motion.

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Law of orbits

lines.text: First law — the law of orbits:

lines: Every planet moves round the sun in an
elliptical orbit, with the sun at one of the
steps.why: The other focus is empty — nothing sits there. That is why an orbit is not symmetric about the sun.
common_mistakes: Saying the sun is at the CENTRE of the ellipse; it is at a focus.

recall.must_convey: That every planet moves in an ellipse with the sun at one focus.
accept: ellipse with the sun at one focus

steps.memory_tip: Orbits: an ellipse with the sun at ONE focus — the other focus is empty.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say focus, not centre, and the sentence is complete.

steps.label: The figure
steps.why: The two shaded sectors are the second law drawn: short and fat near the sun, long and thin far away, and equal in area.
common_mistakes: Drawing a circle, which loses both the foci and the whole point of the first law.

recall.must_convey: That an ellipse is drawn with the sun at one focus and two equal-area sectors marked.
accept: draw the ellipse with the sun at a focus
reject: T squared is proportional to a cubed

steps.memory_tip: Shade two sectors: short and wide near the sun, long and thin far away — equal areas.
steps.margin_note: Second mark is the figure. Ellipse, sun at one focus, two shaded sectors.

steps.label: Law of areas

lines.text: Second law — the law of areas:

lines: The line joining a planet to the sun sweeps out
equal areas in equal intervals of time.
So a planet moves faster when it is nearer the
sun and slower when it is farther away.
steps.why: This law is the conservation of angular momentum in disguise — the sun’s pull has no turning effect about the sun.
common_mistakes: Saying the planet sweeps equal ANGLES in equal times, which is false for an ellipse.

recall.must_convey: That the line joining planet to sun sweeps equal areas in equal times, so d A by d t is constant.
accept: d A by d t is constant
reject: ellipse with the sun at one focus

steps.memory_tip: Areas: equal areas in equal times — conservation of angular momentum in different words.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The areas sentence together with dA/dt = constant.

steps.label: Law of periods

lines.text: Third law — the law of periods:

lines: The square of the time period of a planet is
proportional to the cube of the semi-major
steps.why: This is the law that lets one measured orbit fix the distance of every other planet from the sun.
common_mistakes: Writing T³ ∝ a², with the powers swapped.

recall.must_convey: That T squared is proportional to a cubed, the cube of the semi-major axis.
accept: T squared proportional to a cubed

steps.memory_tip: Periods: T² ∝ a³ — square of the time, cube of the semi-major axis. Learn the three names in order: orbits, areas, periods.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. T² ∝ a³, with a named as the semi-major axis.

insider_note: The law of areas is also asked ALONE as a 2-mark question — be ready to state it by itself.
